entities.name: PMID:25092992
observations: Prospective 6-month study of 60 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin 500 mg/day; pioglitazone 15 mg/day (n=30) was compared with glimepiride 1 mg/day (n=30).
CAVI decreased significantly after 6 months with pioglitazone but remained unchanged with glimepiride; the between-group change was statistically significant.
Baseline CAVI was 9.59±0.88 with pioglitazone and 9.32±1.44 with glimepiride; post-treatment means and exact change values were not reliably available in the retrieved record.

entities.name: Pioglitazone
observations: Added at 15 mg/day for 6 months in metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus; associated with a significant CAVI decrease versus glimepiride in PMID:25092992.

entities.name: Metformin
observations: Background treatment at 500 mg/day in the direct CAVI study of pioglitazone versus glimepiride.

entities.name: Glimepiride
observations: Added at 1 mg/day for 6 months as the comparator to pioglitazone; CAVI remained unchanged.

entities.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
observations: Population in the direct 6-month add-on study evaluating CAVI response to pioglitazone versus glimepiride on metformin.

entities.name: CAVI improvement
observations: In a small prospective study, pioglitazone added to metformin significantly reduced CAVI over 6 months, while glimepiride did not; blood pressure reductions were not significantly different between groups.
Evidence is limited by 30 participants per arm and one principal study, reducing certainty and generalizability.
